original_card.question: Can one known scalar simplification be converted into an actual paid-profile improvement?
methods: Derive the changed legal frame itinerary and exact child histogram.
Prove a scoped obstruction showing why that scalar gain cannot change the paid contract.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An unchanged histogram is not a kappa gain; record any separate runtime or proof benefit explicitly.

first_step.inspect: Observe that the positive control improves scalar counts while retaining the paid histogram.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one simplification and derive the complete changed frame itinerary, or prove why it cannot change the histogram.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legal change to the histogram, not addition count alone, is the bridge to an exponent gain.
allowed_variations: One existing scalar simplification and one proposed frame-path change.
scope_change_triggers: Submitting only another scalar count as completion of a paid-profile task.

actual_scope: On both pinned PR3734 providers, do PR3942's new-gap pruning and same-ADD composition reductions agree with the single-move price oracle at every fixed-frame adjacent pair and every changed first frame?
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether one scalar simplification changes a paid histogram. This package does not propose a new simplification. It audits the obstruction argument in PR #3942, which claims that a radius-one first ADD followed by any second ADD cannot improve the raw rank moment. Discussion #1166 comment 19032637 asks for that independent challenge.
bottleneck_link: A two-ADD scalar retiming improves the exponent only if the rank histogram improves. These reductions say that, inside the stated contract, it does not. A histogram gain has to leave the contract.
stop_rule: Stop after both pinned providers. Do not replay the 11.9-million-row variable census. Stop at the first unlocalized non-bridge price, negative bridge price, disjoint-register frame change, or same-ADD composition mismatch.
evidence: Both providers: 4709 fixed pairs, 1354687 non-bridge gap prices all localized to the original corridor, 14693 bridge prices all curvature-nonnegative, 1047 changed first frames with invariant disjoint-register sequences, and 2609832 same-ADD compositions matching a direct move. Quotient rank at most 3 on 1559 intervals. The trace-free gap rows match candidates() on 47 spread and edge pairs per provider. These counts also match an earlier local exhaustive candidates() pass. No new kappa.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Substantial Cursor Grok assistance. The pinned PR3942 price engine was executed, not rewritten.

open_questions.question: Does one provider's variable_census receipt match PR3942 RESULT-base.json or RESULT-extra.json on the 11,917,718 shared-register second cuts?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This audit checks the reductions that justify skipping most second cuts. It does not re-execute that census, so a bug in the shared-register loop would survive.
open_questions.first_step: Replay search.variable_census for the 29 frame_only_neutral first words only, and compare the histogram with the published rows for that kind.
open_questions.blocked_by: Runtime of the full census, not a missing lemma. The neutral subclass is the bounded first step.

open_questions.question: For one changed first frame on these providers, does a disjoint-register second ADD emit the same cut and dimension deltas before and after that move?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The disjoint-register half of the PR3942 reduction says the final delta is a sum of two original nonnegative deltas. This audit checks that those frame sequences do not change. It does not re-sum a disjoint price.
open_questions.first_step: Pick the first variable move in section A, choose one ADD that shares no register with it, and compare candidates() for that ADD before and after apply_move.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing structural. Open PRs 4122 and 4128 already treat moved illegal intermediates, so this follow-up stays on the disjoint price.
